title: Second look at N-003: the f9v drawing is as described and has no label, so there is no word-to-name pairing to confirm
statement: What I checked on the Yale scan of f9v (canvas 1006093, full page at 1500 pixels). The proposer's description of the drawing holds, with one addition. The plant has five flowers, each of five rounded petals, painted blue in darker and paler tones; two of them, both on the right-hand side, have one lower petal painted yellow instead of blue, which the anchor's statement does not mention (it says blue and pale tones) and which bears on a three-coloured flower as the candidate. Along the stems are narrow, deeply cut green leaves in tufts; at the base are four broad lance-shaped green leaves with toothed edges; the root is a small pale tuft of fine fibres. The text is two blocks of running lines that wrap round the upper flowers, with a few short line-ends between the blossoms; in the pinned ZL transliteration all twelve loci of the page are paragraph lines and none is a label line, which agrees with the proposer's statement that no stand-alone word points at the plant. Why this is a dissent. I do not dispute anything the proposer reports. But an agreeing second look would mark this confirmed, and the record reads confirmed anchors as pairings of a manuscript word with a known name. This entry has neither: its word field and its name fields are empty by the proposer's own choice, and the page offers no label to fill the first. There is nothing here for the test to use, and a confirmed entry with empty fields would overstate what is known. The identification itself I cannot confirm either: I did not open Han, Vatne or the index of early identifications in the time I had, and the proposer notes that the two published discussions compare the drawing with the same botanical plate, which makes them less than two independent identifications. I would keep this as a useful note on the picture (a candidate with reasons and limits) and not as an anchor. If the project's rule is that a wordless picture note may be confirmed as such, this dissent should be read as agreement with the description and overruled.
sources: Zandbergen-Landini transliteration ZL 3b (pinned data/raw/ZL3b-n.txt): f9v has twelve loci, all paragraph lines (unit P0), no label lines
